task.title: How to Connect a Barcode App to a Webpage for Inventory?

user_message.content: Is there a way to connect a bar code app to a webpage app that you create to keep up with inventory ?

status_update.description: Manus is working on your request

assistant_message.content:
Great question! Yes, it is absolutely possible to connect a barcode scanning capability to a web-based inventory management app. Before I dive in or start building, let me ask a few questions to make sure I build exactly what you need:

**1. How do you want to scan barcodes?**
- Using your **phone's camera** directly in the browser (no separate app needed)
- Using a **dedicated barcode scanner app** on your phone that sends data to the web app
- Using a **physical USB/Bluetooth barcode scanner** connected to a computer

**2. What kind of inventory are you tracking?**
- Products in a store or warehouse
- Personal items or assets
- Something else?

**3. What features do you need in the inventory app?**
- Add/remove items by scanning
- Track quantities (stock in / stock out)
- View inventory list and search
- Low-stock alerts
- Export reports (CSV, PDF)?

**4. Do you need user accounts or multi-user access**, or is this just for a single user?

**5. Do you already have barcodes on your items**, or would you also need to generate/print barcodes?

Feel free to answer as many or as few as you'd like — I can also proceed with a sensible default setup (browser-based camera scanning + full inventory management web app) if you'd prefer to just get started!

Here are real examples of QR codes and labels printed on small vials and supplement bottles, along with the top printer recommendations for your standard peptide bottles:

---

## What the Examples Show

**Image 3 (top row, center)** is the most relevant — a standard peptide/supplement vial with a full wrap-around label including a QR code, batch number, expiry date, and storage instructions. This is exactly the format you'd use.

**Images 5 & 6 (bottom row)** show pre-printed sheet labels for 2ml–10ml vials — these are what you'd get from a commercial print run or from a Niimbot/DYMO printer on roll stock.

**Image 4 (top right)** shows the Niimbot M2 printing 50×30mm hologram-style labels for small vials — the QR code is clearly readable even at that small size.

---

## Top Printer Recommendations for Standard Peptide Bottles

| Printer | Price | Label Size | QR Quality | Best For |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Niimbot M2** | ~$100–$140 | 20–50mm wide | ★★★★★ 300 DPI | **Best overall for vials** — specifically designed for small bottles, prints color labels, connects via phone Bluetooth |
| **DYMO LabelWriter 550** | ~$120–$160 | 11mm–59mm wide | ★★★★☆ 300 DPI | Desktop use, fast, great QR sharpness, wide label variety |
| **Brother QL-820NWB** | ~$150–$200 | Up to 62mm wide | ★★★★☆ 300 DPI | High volume, WiFi + Bluetooth, very reliable, good for batches |
| **Phomemo M110** | ~$40–$60 | 15–50mm wide | ★★★☆☆ 203 DPI | Budget option, Bluetooth phone app, decent for basic QR labels |

---

## Key Considerations for Peptide Bottle Labels

**Minimum QR code size for reliable scanning:** A QR code needs to be at least **15mm × 15mm** (about 0.6 inches square) to scan reliably with a phone camera. Anything smaller risks scan failures.

**Label size for standard vials:**
- **2ml vial** → wrap label ~40mm × 15mm or cap label ~13mm round
- **5ml vial** → wrap label ~50mm × 20mm
- **10ml vial** → wrap label ~50mm × 30mm (most common)

**My top recommendation: Niimbot M2** — it was literally designed for vials and small bottles, prints at 300 DPI (sharp QR codes), connects directly to your phone via Bluetooth, and has a dedicated vial label roll size (50×30mm) that wraps perfectly around standard peptide bottles. You can design and print directly from your phone using their app.

**Important:** For peptide bottles that may be stored cold or handled frequently, look for **waterproof/oil-resistant label rolls** — Niimbot sells holographic and waterproof options specifically for vials (as seen in image 4 and 6 above).

---

**Suggested next steps:**
1. I can **resize the QR labels in your app** to output a print-ready 50×30mm label format optimized for the Niimbot M2 or DYMO — just let me know which printer you go with
2. I can **add a batch/lot number and expiry date field** to your product labels so that information prints on the vial label alongside the QR code
3. I can **generate a test label sheet** as a PDF in the exact dimensions of your chosen label stock so you can verify sizing before printing a full batch
